h1: Deferred Adjudication Record Cleanup in El Paso, Texas
intro: Deferred disposition gets your ticket dismissed — but the dismissal doesn't erase the record. Most people never take the last step. Attorney Robert Navar comes back after the deferral is complete and clears the case from your record for good.
summary: After deferred disposition on a Class C ticket, the case is dismissed with no conviction — but the charge, the court file and any arrest or booking record remain on file and can appear on background checks.

Once the deferral is completed and the case dismissed, a Class C deferred disposition is generally eligible for expunction under Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 55A — the records are destroyed, not just hidden.
Misdemeanor deferred adjudication from a county court is handled differently: it is generally sealed with an order of nondisclosure under Government Code Chapter 411.
We bundle multiple old cases into one petition where the law allows, quote a flat fee after a free consultation, and give former ticket clients priority. Call 915-503-1600.

sections.heading: The Step Most Deferred Disposition Clients Never Take
paragraphs: Every week our office resolves El Paso tickets through deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45.051. The client pays a court fee, stays violation-free for 90 to 180 days, and the judge dismisses the case. No conviction, no points. For the speeding ticket itself, that is the finish line.

For your record, it is not. The dismissal does not delete anything. The court's docket still shows the charge and the deferral. If the ticket ever turned into a warrant and you were booked — even for an hour — there is an arrest record at the El Paso Police Department or Sheriff's Office and a matching entry at DPS. Background-check vendors buy that data and show it as "charge: dismissed," which an employer reads as an arrest.

Texas law gives you a fix. Because a Class C offense that was dismissed after deferred disposition is generally eligible for expunction once the deferral is complete, the court can order every agency to destroy those records. Almost nobody does it, because nobody tells them they can.

sections.heading: How We Come Back and Expunge a Class C Deferred Case
paragraphs: When we resolve a ticket with deferred disposition, we calendar the end of the deferral period. Once the court enters the dismissal — in practice, about a year after the original citation by the time the deferral runs and the clerk updates the file — we reach out to the client and offer to finish the job. Former clients of the firm get a reduced flat fee because we already have the citation, the court, the cause number and the dismissal order on file.

The expunction itself is a petition in El Paso County district court at 500 E. San Antonio Ave. It names the court that handled the ticket — El Paso Municipal Court, a Justice of the Peace precinct, or one of the Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint or Anthony courts — plus the arresting agency, DPS and the prosecutor. The court sets a hearing at least 30 days out, the order is signed, and the clerk sends certified copies to each agency for destruction. A typical uncontested petition is finished within a few months.

sections.heading: Misdemeanor Deferred Adjudication: Nondisclosure Instead of Expunction
paragraphs: Class A and B misdemeanors — a first DWLI with a prior, possession of marijuana, theft under $750, assault — are handled in the El Paso County Courts at Law, and the deferral there is called deferred adjudication under art. 42A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Completing it gets the case dismissed without a conviction, but Texas does not allow expunction of a Class A or B deferred adjudication. The remedy is an order of nondisclosure, which seals the case from the public and private background checks while leaving it visible to law enforcement and licensing agencies.

For many first-time, non-violent misdemeanors the court is supposed to issue the order automatically at discharge under Government Code § 411.072. In practice, clients often find it never happened — the fee was not paid, the clerk did not process it, or the case fell outside that section. We check the court file and, if needed, file a petition under § 411.0725 in the same county court. Waiting periods are generally none for most misdemeanors and two years for certain offenses; family-violence findings and a few other categories are excluded. We confirm the current rule before filing.

sections.heading: Bundling Old Cases: One Petition, Several Tickets
paragraphs: Most people who had one ticket had more than one. A no-insurance ticket in 2019, a speeding ticket in Horizon City in 2021, a warrant arrest in 2022 that was later recalled and dismissed. Texas allows a single expunction petition to cover multiple arrests when they are eligible, and the El Paso district courts routinely sign orders that list several cause numbers across several courts. Filing once instead of three times saves filing fees and months of waiting.

The catch is that each case must independently qualify. A ticket that was paid rather than deferred is a conviction and stays. A deferred that was revoked for a new violation during the probation period ended in a conviction and stays. Part of our free review is sorting your history into three piles — expungeable, sealable, and permanent — so you know exactly what we can clear and what it costs before you decide anything.
We pull the DPS record and the court histories ourselves, so you do not need to remember cause numbers.

sections.heading: Who Should Clean Up a Deferred Record Now
paragraphs: If you are applying for anything that runs a background check in El Paso — Fort Bliss civilian jobs, CBP or Border Patrol, a hospital, a school district, a CDL carrier, a security clearance, an apartment — do this before you apply, not after a denial. Expunction takes a few months and the agencies need time to purge their copies. The same goes for immigration filings and professional licenses, where an unexplained "arrest" entry triggers a request for evidence.

Our fee is a flat amount quoted after a free consultation, with a reduced rate for former clients of the firm whose tickets we resolved. Filing fees and certified copies are separate and disclosed up front. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case; eligibility depends on how each case was closed and what has happened since. faqs.q: My ticket was dismissed after deferred disposition. Isn't it already off my record?
faqs.a: The conviction never happened, so it is off your driving record. But the charge, the court file and any arrest record still exist and can appear on background checks as a dismissed charge. An expunction is what actually destroys those records.

faqs.q: How long after finishing deferred disposition can I file for expunction?
faqs.a: A Class C deferred disposition is generally eligible once the deferral is complete and the court has entered the dismissal. We verify the dismissal in the court's file, confirm eligibility against the current statute, and file. In practice the whole cycle from citation to signed expunction is often about a year to eighteen months.

faqs.q: What if I got the deferral and then a new ticket during the probation period?
faqs.a: If the court revoked the deferral and entered a conviction, that case is generally not expungeable. If the new ticket was handled separately and the original deferral still ended in dismissal, the original case usually remains eligible. We check the clerk's record for each case.

faqs.q: Can you expunge a misdemeanor deferred adjudication from county court?
faqs.a: Generally no — Class A and B deferred adjudications are sealed with an order of nondisclosure rather than expunged. For many first-time misdemeanors that order should have been issued automatically at discharge; if it was not, we file the petition in the same county court.

faqs.q: Can several old tickets go in one petition?
faqs.a: Yes, when each is independently eligible. One petition listing multiple cause numbers across El Paso Municipal, JP and area courts is common and saves fees and time. Paid convictions have to be left out.

faqs.q: I was a client of the firm for the ticket. Do you still have my file?
faqs.a: Yes. We keep the citation, court, cause number and dismissal order, which is why former clients get a reduced flat fee and a faster filing. Call 915-503-1600 and we will find it.
